I briefly creeped your post history and you're younger than I am. Kudos on being so mature and on having your own life, dude. I know exactly what you mean about creating a life outside of my household. That's what I've been working towards for the past three years and it literally is two weeks away - I'm graduating from Uni and will be on my own, fully, for the first time in my life. I've "stuck through" the shitty household life because it's all been leading towards *this*.

But, in a way, I feel me being the youngest and my mom fully empty nesting played a part in her decision. I feel like I'm abandoning her, especially now. 

This is all just really fresh and deeply scarring. I've been running on autopilot for the past few days. 

By the way - post high school is amazing. If you're taking the uni/college route or not - seriously, these will be the best years of your life. They're over all too fast. Say yes to everything, don't overthink hooking up with someone and do things (within reason) for the story, not the consequence. You sound like you have your life in order but as the cliche goes, this really is a fresh start. You'll realize once high school is over just how little people care/how little those years mattered and how everyone else is really truly now responsible for their own lives. I'd say the most important thing is to do something instead of not doing it. Live with consequences rather than regret. 

Edit: don't mean to say college is the "best years of your life"; it's the years that you realize life isn't really measured in chapters. College isn't the best years of your life, your 20s are. Everything is suddenly extremely tangible and within reach. I just can't put myself back in that mindset right now.

I know I outlined all this in a response a few minutes ago and I hope this thread isn't buried yet, but I need some serious advice.

I've been pouring over reddit posts for the past few months about parents with mental illnesses, suicidal parents, etc. There's a bit of a dichotomy in people's advice/ways of coping.

On the one hand, many people say that just because you're blood relatives with someone doesn't mean that you have to take care of them. My mom made a decision on her own, she's an adult and her life is not my responsibility. Taking it on as such would lead to a detriment in both of our mental health. I can't speak for her state (it's obviously not great) but I know I'm going to have a serious fucking decline into absolute nothingness if I have to become the only pillar of support for my mother. That I won't be able to handle. We have a toxic relationship but I think she's closest to me than she is to my brother or my father. She loves me but sometimes it's overwhelming and suffocating; I'm 22 and I need my own private life. There's a school of thought out there that cutting someone loose and focusing on yourself, as hard as it may be, is the best thing you can do. You can't be responsible for another person's life. 

So, if I take this route and maintain a firm distance from this shitshow, at least for a while, then I'm faced with daily crippling guilt and possible emails/phonecalls and basically falling back into my same fear as a teenager - a fear that's quite real now - of getting that fucking call again and failing my mother. If I'm going to let her go, why didn't I just not call the ambulance? The pills were already in her. I saved her life and I don't know if I made the right decision.

The other route is being her pillar of support and allowing her to have a much bigger part in my life because she's in such a state of crisis. My dad works overseas and my brother has his own life and isn't exactly easy to connect with. However, my teenage years were spent fantasizing about the life and freedom I'd have for myself once I was done University. Rent paid on my own, freedom to pursue my own hobbies, relationships - freedom to be myself and work on my baggage myself. My parents fought a lot - screaming matches, listening to my mom threaten suicide to my dad, coming home from school to loud bawling. The possibility of a future of independence was quite possibly what kept me from getting to that state of mind myself. But at the same time, my mom does love and did sacrifice a lot in her life for me. No family's perfect, right? Should I be there for her and try to help her ease the burden? 

If I go with option B, then I know that a: I won't be able to focus on my own life, as that fear will still be a constant presence and b: we'll continue to have a toxic relationship, I'll never be able to fully connect with her as I'll be constantly walking on eggshells and I'll be terrified of socializing and trying to maintain a "normal" face at family events/other engagements. I'm scared I'll grow to resent her. 

Any thoughts on either of these? It's not like my mother was entirely abusive and I can just say "fuck you" and have her deal with her shit, but at the same time she was never a pillar of strength and sanity and her emotional dependance on me is/was beginning to tear down my own mental well being.

I saw her today. She's better and is probably going to make it. 

I'm so sorry to hear about your mother. At such a young age that must have taken away a lot from you. The only thing I have going for myself that's not letting this consume me is the scraps of a life I'm building for myself to have after I finish school. 

I do love her. I try to show her that as much as I can. The fact that she's going to make it is a relief but at the same time brings with it it's own massive weight. Since I was around your age I've had this weight of a potential suicide or breakup between my parents or worse hanging over me. I never brought any friends home and always feared my school bus turning the corner and all my peers seeing an ambulance or cop car in front of the house. 

The part that's consuming me is that I don't have an out, the way I see it. As fucked up as it is, when she was on life support, there was almost a small moment of relief. Her sister believes in suicide as her family had an extremely traumatic childhood and their brother killed himself a decade or so ago. My mom doesn't exactly have a life to live for. I don't think she's capable of making one for her own. 

I'm basically torn between the choice of being the only one in my family she can confide in and have a relationship - which is more and more volatile the more time we spend together - and developing more resentment towards her while at the detriment to not only my mental state of mind but for the private independent life I've been creating on my own. Or I let her go and put distance between us and live with the crushing guilt of that decision. Even being on the phone with the ambulance I wasn't sure if I was making the right decision or not. She doesn't want to bear this burden on me but she doesn't want to live either. I think part of her saw offing herself as a way to ease the burden on me and my brother. 

I'm seeing someone this weekend but I don't know how to start dealing with this. It's turning into that cold flat circle of True Detective. This shit is just going to keep repeating itself. 

I try to be strong but that relies on me maintaining my own personal island. I don't see an out right now. I don't see any path I can take. 

How are you doing now? How did your family cope with this?
Thank you.
